references.title: New insights into the biological role of the osmoregulated periplasmic glucans in pathogenic and symbiotic bacteria.

reference_review.review_notes: Full text; comparative review supplies route boundaries, not exact enzyme assignments.

findings.statement: OPG backbone synthesis includes OpgGH-dependent and Ndv/Chv/Cgs-dependent systems; product cyclicity alone does not identify the biosynthetic mechanism.
OPG structural diversity must be retained when sampling taxa; the linear enterobacterial product is one realization.
findings.supporting_text: The OPGs were divided into four families based on their structure

references.title: Enzymes that catalyze cyclization of β-1,2-glucans.

reference_review.review_notes: Full text; recent review integrates the 2023 hydrolase and 2024 cyclase discoveries. Primary papers independently ground chemistry.

findings.statement: OpgG and OpgD have different native genetic phenotypes; chain-length control is separable from loss of OPG synthesis.
findings.supporting_text: A ΔopgD strain produces OPG with main chains longer than those of a wild-type strain.

references.title: Identification of enzymatic functions of osmo-regulated periplasmic glucan biosynthesis proteins from Escherichia coli reveals a novel glycoside hydrolase family.

reference_review.review_notes: Full text; BL21-derived signal-deleted, His-tagged proteins. Exact precursor identity to K-12 is verified separately. Measured activity does not establish the native OpgG reaction.

findings.statement: E. coli OpgG has measurable intrinsic beta-1,2-glucan hydrolysis; weak activity is not evidence that the molecular function is absent.
findings.supporting_text: EcOpgG was found to hydrolyze β-1,2-glucans; however, the catalytic velocity was very low

findings.statement: OpgG hydrolysis is much slower under the reported comparison, so it must not be silently equated with the physiological chain-processing role of OpgD.
Purified E. coli OpgD directly hydrolyzes beta-1,2-glucans; this intrinsic reaction is distinct from the inferred native chain-length mechanism.
findings.supporting_text: EcOpgD exhibited hydrolytic activity toward β-1,2-glucans

references.title: Discovery of Anomer-Inverting Transglycosylase: Cyclic Glucohexadecaose-Producing Enzyme from Xanthomonas, a Phytopathogen.

reference_review.review_notes: Full text; purified recombinant XccOpgD makes a cyclic product. PDB 8X18 source and SIFTS identify ATCC 33913 Q8P3C6; construct details require separate inspection.

findings.statement: XccOpgD alone converts a linear beta-1,2 substrate into the alpha-1,6-closed cyclic hexadecaose; GH186 membership cannot grant hydrolase activity uniformly.
findings.supporting_text:
XccOpgD, a GH186 homologue from X. campestris pv. campestris, alone
converts linear β-1,2-glucan into CβG16α specifically.

references.title: The opgGIH and opgC genes of Rhodobacter sphaeroides form an operon that controls backbone synthesis and succinylation of osmoregulated periplasmic glucans.

reference_review.review_notes: Abstract only at acquisition; genetic participation and complementation are explicit, but exact strain and individual chemical steps need further primary-source verification. Subsequent publisher Table1 inspection identifies 2.4.1 opgG/opgI/opgH mutants; exact sequence provenance is being archived with the gene reviews.

findings.statement: The Rhodobacter pathway requires an additional OpgI component; a universal two-gene criterion would misrepresent this realization.
findings.supporting_text:
Inactivation of opgG, opgI or opgH
abolished OPG production

findings.statement: Rhodobacter genes can yield a different product topology in a heterologous host, so family membership alone does not specify the final product.

references.title: Osmoregulated periplasmic glucans of the free-living photosynthetic bacterium Rhodobacter sphaeroides.

reference_review.review_notes: Abstract only; isolation, mass spectrometry and NMR explicitly characterize the product. This establishes chemistry without assigning an individual enzyme to ring closure. Publisher Figure7 identifies WS8 for the NMR-resolved 18-mer; this is not direct product chemistry on the 2.4.1 gene-panel strain.

findings.statement: The Rhodobacter product predominantly contains eighteen glucose residues, with seventeen beta-1,2 linkages and one alpha-1,6 closure.
findings.supporting_text:
a single alpha-1,6 glycosidic linkage, whereas all other glucose
residues are beta-1,2 linked

references.title: OpgH is an essential regulator of Caulobacter morphology.

reference_review.review_notes: Full text; NA1000 CCNA_02097 matches B8GX72. Morphology, active-site mutation and substrate accumulation support a functional inference; direct product detection failed.

findings.statement: Caulobacter provides an OpgH-only comparative boundary, not a demonstrated complete OpgGH product-synthesis witness.
findings.supporting_text: the only opg homolog encoded in Caulobacter is opgH (CCNA_02097)

findings.statement: Failure of the E. coli isolation method to detect the Caulobacter product leaves its chemistry unresolved; it does not prove product absence.
findings.supporting_text: we were unable to detect OPGs using these methods

references.title: Homology between a genetic locus (mdoA) involved in the osmoregulated biosynthesis of periplasmic glucans in Escherichia coli and a genetic locus (hrpM) controlling pathogenicity of Pseudomonas syringae.

references.title: Biosynthesis of membrane-derived oligosaccharides. Membrane-bound glucosyltransferase system from Escherichia coli requires polyprenyl phosphate.

references.title: Identification of mdoD, an mdoG paralog which encodes a twin-arginine-dependent periplasmic protein that controls osmoregulated periplasmic glucan backbone structures.

reference_review.review_notes: Cached abstract inspected; claims are limited to the stated membrane-system, localization or genetic result. Exact construct/strain details not in the abstract are not supplied from memory.

findings.statement: OpgD affects native OPG chain lengths; its loss does not abolish all OPG production.
findings.supporting_text: mdoD resulted in production of OPGs with a higher degree of polymerization

references.title: An essential function for acyl carrier protein in the biosynthesis of membrane-derived oligosaccharides of Escherichia coli.

reference_review.review_notes: Cached abstract inspected. For2945202 the publisher PDF additionally distinguishes K-12 purified factor from DF214 membrane preparations; scoped source and comparator evidence is in the AcpP source analysis. No autonomous ACP glucosyltransferase or universal family compatibility is asserted.

findings.statement: Purified ACP substitutes for the soluble factor and antibody inhibition is reversed by added ACP, supporting direct cofactor participation in the membrane glucan reaction.
findings.supporting_text:
Antibody raised against pure ACP completely inhibits
transglucosylation activity
